question.text: This date titles a Francisco Goya painting showing a firing squad and a group of prisoners. The work depicts a scene during an 1808 invasion.
question.answerHtml: May 3rd (or 5/3; accept The Third of May 1808 or El tres de mayo de 1808 en Madrid)

swap.leadin: Any member of this political body would immediate dissolve it with the words "I do not allow," the Liberum veto. --.
swap.text: Name this parliamentary body of an eastern European "commonwealth."
swap.clue: The szlachta class composed the majority of its Chamber of Deputies.

question.leadin: It was partitioned several times in the late 18th century.
question.text: Name this region whose king Jan Sobieski III dispersed the Ottomans during the Second Siege of Vienna, which became a modern-day country with its capital at Warsaw.
question.clue: In this country and its eastern neighbor, Jews were finally granted rights to habeas corpus in the Third of May Constitution, which was promulgated by its king Stanislaw Augustus.

swap.leadin: Name these tactics of parliamentary obstructionism.
swap.text: In the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, a member of the Sejm ("Say-m") could enact this type of veto by shouting "I do not allow!" This veto contributed to the Commonwealth's downfall.
swap.clue: The increasing frequency of this action led to the creation of so-called "confederated" bodies where this action was not allowed.

question.leadin: This largest Polish trade union emerged from the Lenin Shipyards.
question.text: Name this trade union formed in the socialist state of Poland that became the name of a social movement against communist ideology in the Eastern Bloc.
question.clue: It rose directly out of the KOR, while its rural branch was led by Jan Kulaj.

swap.leadin: Vytautas the Great was one ruler of this country.
swap.text: Name this country which joined with its western neighbor in the 1569 Union of Lublin. In the 20th century, this Baltic state was the first to declare its independence from the Soviet Union.
swap.answerHtml: Grand Duchy of Lithuania (accept Republic of Lithuania or Lietuvos Respublika)
swap.clue: Algirdas's victory over the Golden Horde at the Battle of Blue Waters drove the greatest expansionary period of this polity, whose ruler Vytautus's involvement with the Samogitian uprisings and incessant warring with the Teutonic Knights helped prompt the Battle of Grunwald. For 15 points, identify this Grand Duchy which participated in the 1569 Union of Lublin.

question.text: In spring 1940, Stalin approved a mass execution at this site, at which about 22,000 Polish nationals and prisoners of war were killed by the Soviet NKVD.

swap.text: This adorable bear was purchased by Polish soldiers during World War II, being taught to move artillery and apparently enjoying eating cigarettes. His name is a diminutive for "joyful warrior."
swap.clue: This Syrian Brown Bear who fought with the Polish II Corps and famously carried 100 pound cases of artillery across the battlefield.

question.leadin: Answer the following regarding the creation of the present unified Germany, per part.
question.text: The German-Polish border was finalized in 1990, with the Germans relinquishing their claim to this city, birthplace of the Solidarity movement.
question.clue: Woodrow Wilson's insistence that a country have access to the sea resulted in the creation of this city's namesake "corridor," which made East Prussia an exclave.

swap.text: Stanislaus's daughter had married Louis XV, but he was sent to Lorraine by the French. The Spanish and Sardinians sought to undo the Peace of Utrecht, and therefore allied with the French against the Germans and Russians. For 15 points-name this 1733 to 1735 conflict which ended with confirmation of Augustus III's reign.
swap.clue: The person who led the Confederation of Dzikow had previously held the job in question under Swedish domination and was the father-in-law of Louis XV.

question.leadin: This man represented opposition groups at the Round Table Talks.
question.text: Name this electrician who led the trade union Solidarity.
question.clue: The KOR ("K-O-R") was a predecessor to an organization led by this man, which formed a coalition government with the PUWP.

swap.leadin: Throughout much of the 16th and 17th centuries, this was the largest state in Europe.
swap.text: Name this polity, which was created through the union of a kingdom at one time ruled by the Piast dynasty with the last European state to accept Christianity.
swap.clue: Monarchs agreed to the Henrician Articles and made individual commitments called the pacta conventa on becoming rulers of this country.

question.text: This king was victorious over the Ottomans at Chocim and at the Battle of the Kahlenberg, lifting the siege of Vienna in 1683, making him surely the most pivotal ruler from the house of Sobieski.
question.answerHtml: Jan III Sobieski (or John III, prompt on Jan)
question.clue: His victory at Chocim coincided with the death of his predecessor Michael I, allowing him to take power.

swap.text: This son of Augustus the Strong was the sitting king of Saxony and emerged from the war with both the Dzikow Confederation and the Treaty of Vienna supporting his ascension to the Polish throne.

question.leadin: This house lost power after the death of Casimir III the Great, the son of Wladyslaw the Elbow-High.
question.text: Name this dynasty founded by Mieszko I that ruled an oft-partitioned country in eastern Europe.

swap.leadin: This ruler defeated the Yaroslav the Wise at the Battle of Bug River and his long war with Henry II was ended with the Peace of Bautzen.
swap.text: Name this member of the Piast Dynasty that established the Prince's Law and was succeeded by Mieszko II.
swap.answerHtml: Bolesław I Chrobry (prompt on “Bolesław”; accept Bolesław the Great; accept Bolesław the Valiant; accept Bolesław the Brave; accept Bolesław Chrobry)
swap.clue: This ruler redeemed the corpse of Saint Adalbert for a sack of gold, and was given a supposed copy of the Holy Lance known as St. Maurice's Spear at the Congress of Gniezno.

question.text: Sobieski came to the throne at the end of this chaotic period in Polish history. It began roughly with the Khmelnytsky Uprising and included an invasion of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth by Sweden.
question.clue: The King-Crane Commission originally suggested that the United States be given control over it, while the St. James Conference rejected the plan for its division set forth by the Peel Commission.

swap.text: This 1915 battle near Osowiec ("oh-SOH-v'yets") Fortress got its name from the fact that a regiment of Russians, many of whom were coughing up bits of lung after being gassed, successfully surprise-assaulted Germans nearly ten times their number.
swap.answerHtml: Attack of the Dead Men [or Ataka Mertvetsov or Kampf der toten Männer; prompt on partial answers]

question.leadin: This man argued that it is "better to have a friend than a slave" in his seminal Essay on Diplomacy, which he wrote under the pseudonym "Philhellene" ("feel-eh-LEN").
question.text: Name this man who founded the Historical and Literary Society in Paris. This man bought the Hotel Lambert, which lends its name to a faction of people led by this man that participated in the Great Emigration.

swap.leadin: A political period sometimes named for this man followed a series of worker protests in Poznan shortly after Boleslaw ("BO-luh-swaf") Bierut's death.
swap.text: . Name this Communist leader who presided over a relative cultural thaw after the Polish October.
swap.clue: Poland also erupted in student protests over the censorship of free speech, which prompted this First Secretary of the Polish United Workers' Party to crack down with an anti-Semitic campaign.
